QUANTITY BEING MEASURED
How many new vulnerabilities will CISA add to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog between May 1, 2026 and May 31, 2026?

RESOLUTION CRITERIA
This question resolves as the number of vulnerabilities in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog with a "Date Added" field between May 1, 2026 and May 31, 2026, inclusive. The count is determined by consulting the official CISA KEV catalog at https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog and filtering by the "Date Added" column. Each unique vulnerability entry (CVE) with a Date Added in the specified range counts as one. The count should be taken on or after June 1, 2026, once the full month of May data is available.

BACKGROUND AVAILABLE AS OF 2026-05-02 14:08:23.377361
CISA maintains the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, a continuously updated list of vulnerabilities that have been observed being actively exploited in the wild. Recent additions to the catalog in late April and early May 2026 include: 7 vulnerabilities on April 13, 1 on April 16, 8 on April 20, 4 on April 24, 2 on April 28, and 1 on May 1, 2026. The pace of additions varies significantly from week to week.

CISA faces significant budget uncertainty. A proposed $491 million cut for FY2026 and a further proposed $707 million cut for FY2027 could reduce CISA's operational capacity, potentially affecting the rate at which new vulnerabilities are processed and added to the KEV catalog. Staff reductions associated with these budget pressures add further uncertainty to whether CISA can maintain its current operational tempo.

TARGET INFORMATION SET
Make a retrospective probability judgment using all information supplied in this prompt, including any LATER RESOLUTION PACKET.

LATER RESOLUTION PACKET
The question resolves to the count of unique CVE entries with a "Date Added" between May 1, 2026 and May 31, 2026 (inclusive) in the official CISA KEV catalog (https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

I reconstructed the count from CISA's official "CISA Adds [N] Known Exploited Vulnerabilit(ies) to Catalog" alerts, which each state exactly how many CVEs were added on a given date. The CISA Cybersecurity Alerts & Advisories listing [Cybersecurity Alerts & Advisories - CISA](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories?f%5B0%5D=advisory_type%3A93) and the US-CERT Current Activity aggregator mirroring CISA alerts [US CERT Current Activity - Information Security - Cal Poly](https://security.calpoly.edu/aggregator/sources/2) both yield the identical per-date breakdown:

- May 1, 2026: 1
- May 6, 2026: 1
- May 7, 2026: 1
- May 8, 2026: 1
- May 14, 2026: 1
- May 15, 2026: 1
- May 20, 2026: 7 (CISA Adds Seven... alert; these are the 7 CVEs dated 2026-05-20, including older CVEs such as CVE-2008-4250, CVE-2009-1537, CVE-2009-3459, CVE-2010-0249, CVE-2010-0806, plus 2026 CVEs)
- May 21, 2026: 2
- May 22, 2026: 1
- May 26, 2026: 1
- May 27, 2026: 3
- May 29, 2026: 1

Sum = 1+1+1+1+1+1+7+2+1+1+3+1 = 21.

There were no "CISA Adds...KEV" alerts on other May dates (no entries May 2–5, May 9–13, May 16–19, May 23–25, May 28, May 30–31). Note: a May 28, 2026 supply-chain compromise advisory (Nx Console/GitHub) was NOT a KEV-addition alert and is correctly excluded.

Both official-source reconstructions independently agree on 21, giving high confidence. admissible_variant.with_information_prompt:
FORECASTING QUESTION
Will the resolved value be strictly less than 9 districts?

QUANTITY BEING MEASURED
How many of the 16 majority districts will the PRI-UDC coalition win in the 2026 Coahuila State Congress election?

RESOLUTION CRITERIA
This question resolves as the number of majority districts (distritos de mayoría relativa) won by the "Alianza Ciudadana por la Seguridad" coalition (PRI-UDC) in the 2026 Coahuila State Congress election held on June 7, 2026. "Majority districts" refers to the 16 single-member districts decided by first-past-the-post voting (mayoría relativa), as distinct from the 9 proportional representation (representación proporcional) seats. The "PRI-UDC coalition" refers specifically to candidates registered under the "Alianza Ciudadana por la Seguridad" banner, which includes the Partido Revolucionario Institucional (PRI) and Unidad Democrática de Coahuila (UDC). A district counts as won if the coalition's candidate receives the most votes in that district. The resolution source is the official results published by the Instituto Electoral de Coahuila (IEC) at https://www.iec.org.mx/.

BACKGROUND AVAILABLE AS OF 2026-05-16 03:43:54.880209
On June 7, 2026, Coahuila will hold elections to renew its State Congress. Of the 25 seats, 16 are elected by majority vote in single-member districts (distritos de mayoría relativa) and 9 by proportional representation. The PRI-UDC coalition, formally registered as "Alianza Ciudadana por la Seguridad" (comprising PRI, UDC, and allied parties), is competing against the Morena-PT coalition and other parties across all 16 majority districts.

According to polling data published by La Encuesta.mx on April 8, 2026, the PRI-UDC coalition leads in 10 of the 16 majority districts, while Morena-PT leads in the remaining 6. However, several races are extremely competitive and within the margin of error — for example, in Distrito 7 the gap is roughly 44.4% vs. 43.3%, and in Distrito 10 it is approximately 42.3% vs. 41.2%. This means the final outcome could plausibly range from around 8 to 12 districts for PRI-UDC depending on which close races break which way. PRI benefits from incumbent institutional advantages (the current governor of Coahuila is from PRI), while Morena has strong national momentum.

TARGET INFORMATION SET
Make a retrospective probability judgment using all information supplied in this prompt, including any LATER RESOLUTION PACKET.

LATER RESOLUTION PACKET
The question asks how many of the 16 majority (mayoría relativa) districts the PRI-UDC coalition "Alianza Ciudadana por la Seguridad" won in the June 7, 2026 Coahuila State Congress election. The answer is 16 — the coalition swept all 16 single-member districts.

Evidence:
- Official IEC district-level cómputos results (Instituto Electoral de Coahuila), published at https://iecoah.org.mx/resultados-computos-pel-2025-2026/, show the PRI (lead party of the "Alianza Ciudadana por la Seguridad" coalition with UDC) receiving the most votes in all 16 districts (Distritos 1–16), i.e. the coalition won all 16 [https://iecoah.org.mx/resultados-computos-pel-2025-2026/](https://iecoah.org.mx/resultados-computos-pel-2025-2026/). This is the IEC's official final cómputos-distritales results page. (Note: the resolution criteria cite https://www.iec.org.mx/; the IEC's live 2026 results are hosted on the institute's current domain iecoah.org.mx, whereas the legacy iec.org.mx/v1 site only lists historical processes and did not contain the 2026 results [Conteo Rapido - Instituto Electoral de Coahuila](https://iec.org.mx/v1/index.php/conteo-rapido).)
- The IEC finalized its Cómputos Distritales at 22:32 on Wednesday June 10, 2026, and issued the constancias de mayoría; the Cómputo Estatal was approved June 14, 2026 (IEC.CG.137.2026).
- El País (June 8, 2026) reports the IEC completed counting of all 4,019 actas and that the "Alianza Ciudadana por la Seguridad" (PRI-UDC) won all 16 majority districts with ~684,515 votes (55%), while the Morena-PT coalition won none [El PRI arrasa en Coahuila y conserva su bastión frente a un Morena ...](https://elpais.com/mexico/2026-06-08/el-pri-arrasa-en-coahuila-y-conserva-su-bastion-frente-a-un-morena-debilitado.html).
- Milenio (PREP, 100% of actas) lists the winning candidates for each of Distritos 1–16, all belonging to the PRI-UDC coalition [Alianza PRI-UDC gana en 16 distritos de Coahuila, según PREP](https://www.milenio.com/elecciones/prep-da-ventaja-pri-udc-eleccion-diputados-locales-coahuila).
- Spanish Wikipedia, citing the official IEC results, likewise reports the coalition won all 16 majority districts (14 PRI + 2 UDC in the district breakdown) [Elecciones estatales de Coahuila de 2026 - Wikipedia](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elecciones_estatales_de_Coahuila_de_2026).

All sources agree unanimously on 16 of 16. Only the 9 proportional-representation seats are excluded from this count, per the resolution criteria, and they do not affect the majority-district total.

In 2025, a total of 41,472 people were detected crossing the Channel in small boats, a 13% increase over 2024 and the second-highest annual figure on record [Tracking UK migration: Small boats, asylum hotels and visas - BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c70989jrdweo).

May 2025 was a notably active month for crossings. On 31 May 2025 alone, 1,195 people crossed the Channel in 19 small boats—the highest single-day figure recorded in 2025. By the end of May 2025, the cumulative year-to-date total had surpassed 15,000 people.

As of 26 April 2026, a total of 6,326 people had crossed the English Channel by small boat since the start of the year, which was down 34% compared to the same period in 2025 [Tracking UK migration: Small boats, asylum hotels and visas - BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c70989jrdweo). The most recent weekly figure showed 941 arrivals for the week ending 19 April 2026 [Weekly summary of small boat arrivals and preventions - GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/migrants-detected-crossing-the-english-channel-in-small-boats/weekly-summary-of-small-boat-arrivals-and-preventions). Crossing volumes are influenced by weather conditions, enforcement activities, migrant flows, and policy changes including the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Act (2025).

An initial automated count of 2,812 used an incorrect end-of-April baseline (dropping the 27-30 April crossings) and mis-summed early May.

How many justices will be in the majority in the U.S. Supreme Court's opinion in Hamm v. Smith (24-872)?

RESOLUTION CRITERIA
This question resolves as the number of justices in the majority opinion in Hamm v. Smith (No. 24-872), as reported in the official opinion published on supremecourt.gov.

The "majority" is defined as the number of justices who join or author the opinion of the Court (the judgment-controlling opinion). A justice who concurs in the judgment only, or who concurs in part and dissents in part, is NOT counted in the majority for purposes of this question — only justices who fully join the majority opinion or the relevant controlling section count.

Specifically:
- If the opinion is a standard majority opinion, count all justices who join it in full.
- If a justice concurs in part and dissents in part, that justice is NOT counted in the majority. Only justices joining the majority opinion in full are counted.
- If there is no single majority opinion (i.e., a plurality), count the number of justices joining the plurality opinion.
- If a justice is recused, the total number of participating justices is reduced accordingly.
- If the case is Dismissed as Improvidently Granted (DIG), this question resolves as 0 (zero).

Source: The official slip opinion published at https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/slipopinion/25 for the October 2025 Term.

The "majority" is defined as the number of justices who join or author the opinion of the Court (the judgment-controlling opinion). A justice who concurs in the judgment only, or who concurs in part and dissents in part, is NOT counted in the majority for purposes of this question — only justices who fully join the majority opinion or the relevant controlling section count.

Specifically:

- If a justice concurs in part and dissents in part, that justice is NOT counted in the majority. Only justices joining the majority opinion in full are counted.
- If there is no single majority opinion (i.e., a plurality), count the number of justices joining the plurality opinion.
- If a justice is recused, the total number of participating justices is reduced accordingly.

- If only April 2026 data is available by July 1, 2026, the question resolves as that single month's UAE remittance figure.
- If no data for any of the three months has been published by July 1, 2026, the question resolves ambiguously (N/A).

According to the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), UAE remittances to Pakistan were $696.2 million in February 2026 and rose to $823.7 million in March 2026 [[PDF] Press Release of Workers' Remittances for March 2026](https://www.sbp.org.pk/press/2026/Pr-08-Apr-2026.pdf). Recent monthly figures (FY2026) have generally ranged between $650 million and $850 million from the UAE.

Reports indicate that mass deportations of Pakistani workers from the UAE began in mid-April 2026, raising concerns about a potential sharp decline in remittance flows. Frozen savings and disrupted employment could reduce the volume of money sent home. This question tracks whether these disruptions materially reduce UAE-to-Pakistan remittance flows during the April–June 2026 window.

TARGET INFORMATION SET
Make a retrospective probability judgment using all information supplied in this prompt, including any LATER RESOLUTION PACKET.

The question resolves as the lowest single-month UAE→Pakistan remittance figure among April, May, and June 2026, using the SBP "Press Release of Workers' Remittances" series, with data available by July 1, 2026.

- April 2026 data: published in SBP press release Pr-11-May-2026.pdf (https://www.sbp.org.pk/press/2026/Pr-11-May-2026.pdf), released ~May 11, 2026.
- May 2026 data: published in SBP press release Pr-10-Jun-2026.pdf (https://www.sbp.org.pk/press/2026/Pr-10-Jun-2026.pdf), released Wednesday, June 10, 2026 [Saudi Arabia leads as Pakistan records highest-ever monthly ...](https://www.arabnews.pk/node/2646617/pakistan).
- June 2026 data: NOT published before July 1, 2026 (SBP releases data ~10–15 days after month-end, so June data would appear ~July 10, 2026). This matches the resolution criteria's "most likely scenario," so resolution = minimum of the two available months (April and May).

UAE figures:
- April 2026 UAE remittances = US$734.7 million. The SBP April press release (Pr-11-May-2026.pdf) states inflows were "mainly sourced from Saudi Arabia ($841.7 million), United Arab Emirates ($734.7 million), United Kingdom ($563.7 million)…" — as reproduced by Pakistani outlets citing SBP (The Nation, Pak Observer). Mettis Global, citing SBP, reported the more precise $734.74 million (down 11.5% m/m from March's $829.91m, up 12.6% y/y from $652.61m in April 2025) [Workers' Remittances hits $3.54bn in April 2026 - Mettis Global](https://mettisglobal.news/Workers-Remittances-hits-354bn-in-April-2026-60338). Business Recorder reported the rounded $735 million (up 13% y/y from $653m in April 2025) [Pakistan records $3.5bn in remittances for April 2026 - Markets](https://www.brecorder.com/news/40420564/pakistan-records-35bn-in-remittances-for-april-2026).
- May 2026 UAE remittances = ~US$1,007 million (Arab News, citing SBP: "The United Arab Emirates followed closely with $1.007 billion") [Saudi Arabia leads as Pakistan records highest-ever monthly ...](https://www.arabnews.pk/node/2646617/pakistan); the SBP May press release states UAE at US$1,006.6 million.

Note on the deportation narrative: the question's description raised concern that mid-April 2026 mass deportations of Pakistani workers from the UAE could sharply cut remittances. This does not affect resolution, which is purely the reported minimum.

Precision note: I report 734.7 because the resolution criteria specify "the country-specific UAE remittance amount in millions of US dollars as reported in the SBP press release," and the SBP press release states $734.7 million. Mettis's $734.74m is a slightly more precise rendering of the same figure; Business Recorder's $735m is the rounded value. Any of these represent the same underlying April 2026 UAE datapoint.

The 2022 primary featured competitive races for governor and U.S. Senate.

Early voting for the 2026 primary began on April 27, 2026, and set a first-day record with 35,352 in-person votes cast — a 29% increase over the 2022 primary's first-day figure of 27,298 [First Day of Early Voting Sees Record Turnout | Georgia Secretary of ...](https://sos.ga.gov/news/first-day-early-voting-sees-record-turnout). As of late April 2026, more than 71,000 ballots had been cast including absentee votes. The 2026 primary features competitive races for governor and U.S. Senate. However, early voting surges do not always translate into proportional increases in total turnout, as some voters shift from Election Day to early voting rather than representing net new participation.

TARGET INFORMATION SET
Make a retrospective probability judgment using all information supplied in this prompt, including any LATER RESOLUTION PACKET.

LATER RESOLUTION PACKET
The resolution criteria specify the Georgia Secretary of State Election Data Hub - Unofficial Turnout page at https://sos.ga.gov/page/election-data-hub-unofficial-turnout and the figure labeled "Total Turnout" for the May 19, 2026 Georgia primary. I used that Georgia Secretary of State page as the primary source location; the page is the correct Election Data Hub - Unofficial Turnout URL, though the static text capture available to the document tool did not render the embedded interactive turnout dashboard where the figure is displayed [https://sos.ga.gov/page/election-data-hub-unofficial-turnout](https://sos.ga.gov/page/election-data-hub-unofficial-turnout) [Election Data Hub - Unofficial Turnout | Georgia Secretary of State](https://sos.ga.gov/page/election-data-hub-unofficial-turnout). Because the embedded dashboard text was not exposed in the static capture, I corroborated the dashboard value through indexed copies/snippets of posts explicitly referring to the Georgia Secretary of State Election Hub / Election Data Hub and showing the dashboard line "TOTAL TURNOUT: 2,059,528"; the relevant URLs surfaced were https://www.instagram.com/p/DYm061ajZbx/, https://www.instagram.com/reel/DXroZ_TCU1M/, and https://www.facebook.com/roughdraftatl/posts/georgias-may-19th-primary-election-had-some-record-breaking-turnout-numbersbut-h/1696399751451699/. Thus the numeric value to report, with commas removed as required, is 2059528.

**Definition of 'Jewish visitors':** Individuals counted as entering the Temple Mount via the Mughrabi Bridge (the sole entry point for non-Muslims) during the hours designated for non-Muslim visitation, as tracked and reported by the activist organization Beyadenu – Returning to the Temple Mount or by Israeli Police.

If Beyadenu has not reported and media sources conflict, the earliest published figure from the highest-ranked outlet in the hierarchy above is used.

**If the Temple Mount is closed:** If the Temple Mount is fully closed to non-Muslim visitors for the entirety of Shavuot 2026 (all three days), the question resolves as 0. If it is closed for only part of the holiday, the count reflects only the days/hours it was open.

**If no data is available:** If no source in the hierarchy above publishes a visitor count by June 1, 2026, the question is annulled.

How many separate days during May 1–31, 2026 will the IMD issue a 'Red' color-coded heatwave warning for any part of India?

RESOLUTION CRITERIA
This question resolves as the total number of calendar days within May 1–31, 2026 (inclusive) on which the IMD's "All India Weather Summary and Forecast Bulletin" (published at https://mausam.imd.gov.in) or the "All India Impact Based Weather Warning Bulletin" (archived at https://ndma.gov.in) includes a 'Red' color warning (meaning "Take Action") for heatwave or severe heatwave conditions for any district or state in India.

A day counts if the warning bulletin published on that date assigns a Red color warning for heatwave/severe heatwave conditions to any part of India for any forecast day. The count is based on the publication date of the bulletin, not the forecast valid dates. For example, if the bulletin published on May 5 includes a Red warning for heatwave conditions (even if valid for May 6 or 7), May 5 is counted.

Each calendar date is counted at most once regardless of how many states or regions receive a Red warning on that date. The final count is determined by reviewing all 31 daily bulletins for May 2026.

As of May 10, 2026, EU natural gas storage levels stand at 35.4% full [Gas storage levels EU - Energy Dashboard](https://energiedashboard.admin.ch/gas/eu-gasspeicher). Storage levels were historically low at approximately 28–29% on April 1, 2026, the lowest since 2018. The Strait of Hormuz crisis has significantly disrupted global LNG flows, with Iran's closure of the strait shutting down major LNG export hubs including Qatar's Ras Laffan facility. This has caused European gas prices to spike 39–50% and created substantial uncertainty around the EU's ability to refill storage ahead of the November 90% target mandated by EU regulation. The injection season is underway, with storage rising roughly 7 percentage points over the past ~40 days, but the pace of refilling depends critically on whether the Strait of Hormuz reopens, LNG rerouting options, pipeline flows, weather-driven demand, and broader geopolitical developments. As of May 12, 2026, the EU aggregate storage level was 35.57% [https://agsi.gie.eu/](https://agsi.gie.eu/).

Direct AGSI+ read: The AGSI+ platform (https://agsi.gie.eu/) showed the EU aggregate at 48.86% Full for the gas day of June 30, 2026 [https://agsi.gie.eu/](https://agsi.gie.eu/). Because the run date is July 1, 2026 and AGSI+ data carries a one-day publishing lag, June 30, 2026 is the most recent preceding day's value — exactly what the resolution criteria instruct using when July 1 is unavailable.

Corroboration (all AGSI/GIE-derived): EnergyRiskIQ, which mirrors AGSI+/GIE data, displayed an "EU Storage %" of 48.9% for its July 1, 2026 snapshot (last updated June 30, 2026) [Europe Gas Storage Levels Today (Updated Daily) | EnergyRiskIQ](https://energyriskiq.com/gas-storage-levels-in-europe), matching 48.86% to rounding. This is further supported by contemporaneous reporting that EU storage was "around 48% full" in late June 2026 (Trading Economics; united24media; nv.ua citing GIE data — found via Google search), consistent with the crisis scenario of depleted, slowly-refilling storage described in the question (35.4% on May 10; 35.57% on May 12).

Reliability note: The AGSI+ dynamic (JavaScript-rendered) sub-pages returned unreliable/inconsistent numbers when queried — one read of https://agsi.gie.eu/data-overview/EU returned ~77% [https://agsi.gie.eu/data-overview/EU](https://agsi.gie.eu/data-overview/EU), which is clearly a hallucination/typical-year artifact, since it is grossly inconsistent with (a) the AGSI+ homepage read of 48.86% [https://agsi.gie.eu/](https://agsi.gie.eu/), (b) EnergyRiskIQ's 48.9% [Europe Gas Storage Levels Today (Updated Daily) | EnergyRiskIQ](https://energyriskiq.com/gas-storage-levels-in-europe), and (c) every independent news source reporting ~48%. The AGSI+ API endpoint returned no data for the range [https://agsi.gie.eu/api?country=eu&from=2026-06-25&to=2026-07-01](https://agsi.gie.eu/api?country=eu&from=2026-06-25&to=2026-07-01), and Bruegel's dataset (last updated June 3, 2026) only reached 37% [European natural gas imports - Bruegel](https://www.bruegel.org/dataset/european-natural-gas-imports). I therefore relied on the two mutually-consistent AGSI-derived reads (48.86% / 48.9%) plus multiple ~48% news corroborations.

What will be the percentage change in BeOne Medicines' stock price (ticker: ONC) from the trading day before the FDA's sonrotoclax PDUFA decision to 3 trading days after?

RESOLUTION CRITERIA
This question resolves as the percentage change in BeOne Medicines' (NASDAQ: ONC) Adjusted Close price between:

1. **Pre-decision price**: The Adjusted Close price on the last trading day immediately before the FDA announcement date (the "decision date").
2. **Post-decision price**: The Adjusted Close price on the third full trading day after the decision date.

The percentage change is calculated as: ((Post-decision price − Pre-decision price) / Pre-decision price) × 100.

**Determining the decision date**: The decision date is the calendar date on which the FDA publicly announces its decision regarding the sonrotoclax NDA. If the FDA announces its decision on a weekend or U.S. federal holiday, the decision date is that calendar date, and the "third full trading day after" is counted from the next regular NASDAQ trading day (which counts as day 1). If the announcement occurs after NASDAQ market close (4:00 PM ET) on a trading day, that trading day is treated as the pre-decision day, and the next trading day counts as day 1.

**Price source**: Adjusted Close prices as reported on Yahoo Finance (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ONC/history/) will be used. "Adjusted Close" accounts for stock splits and dividends.

**Example with PDUFA date of May 26, 2026 (Tuesday)**: If the FDA announces on May 26 during market hours, the pre-decision price is the Adjusted Close on May 22 (Friday, the prior trading day). The three post-decision trading days are May 27, 28, and 29. The post-decision price is the Adjusted Close on May 29 (Thursday).

If the FDA has not issued a decision on sonrotoclax by June 1, 2026, this question is annulled.

Units = "personnel" (absolute scale), so the reported value is 998.

RESOLUTION CRITERIA
This question resolves as the number of weekly US prescriptions for Foundayo (orforglipron) for the week ending May 16, 2026, as reported by IQVIA or Symphony Health. Because IQVIA and Symphony Health prescription data is proprietary, the resolution value will be determined from the earliest credible public report of this data — including media reports (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, STAT News), sell-side analyst notes, or Eli Lilly's own disclosures that cite IQVIA or Symphony Health as the data source. Eli Lilly's oral weight-loss drug Foundayo (orforglipron) received FDA approval on April 1, 2026, and launched in early April 2026. As of mid-April 2026, Foundayo recorded approximately 4,000 prescriptions in its second week on the market [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/eli-lilly-investors-are-eager-foundayo-insight-after-early-launch-data-2026-04-29/](https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/eli-lilly-investors-are-eager-foundayo-insight-after-early-launch-data-2026-04-29/). For comparison, the oral version of Novo Nordisk's Wegovy achieved over 18,000 prescriptions in its first full week, suggesting Foundayo's launch trajectory has been slower [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/eli-lilly-investors-are-eager-foundayo-insight-after-early-launch-data-2026-04-29/](https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/eli-lilly-investors-are-eager-foundayo-insight-after-early-launch-data-2026-04-29/). That figure was publicly reported by June 1, 2026: FiercePharma's Oral GLP-1 Tracker and Citi (citing IQVIA) put it at 'nearly 17,000', and the precise IQVIA tally was 16,698 (week-by-week progression 7,335 -> 10,248 -> 16,698 confirms this). An initial automated fallback to the week-ending-May-22 figure (Jefferies' ~11,700 'best-estimate', vs Citi's ~16,000 for the same week) is wrong because the criteria's fallback only triggers if no week-ending-May-16 data exists, and the corresponding IQVIA week (May 15) was in fact reported. Answer is in plain prescription counts: 16698.

How many English local council seats will the Green Party win in the May 2026 local elections?

RESOLUTION CRITERIA
This question resolves as the total number of English local council seats won by the Green Party of England and Wales in the 7 May 2026 local elections, as reported by the BBC News "Local Elections 2026" England results page (https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2026/england/results). The count includes all seats won across all types of councils holding elections on that date (metropolitan boroughs, London boroughs, unitary authorities, county councils, and district councils). If the BBC results page is unavailable or incomplete, PA Media (Press Association) aggregate results shall be used as the fallback source.

BACKGROUND AVAILABLE AS OF 2026-05-02 11:35:15.261471
The 2026 English local elections are scheduled for 7 May 2026, with 5,066 council seats contested across 136 local authorities, including 32 London borough councils, 32 metropolitan boroughs, 18 unitary authorities, 6 county councils, and 48 district councils [2026 United Kingdom local elections - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_Kingdom_local_elections). The Green Party currently holds 914 seats, with 170 of those up for election in this cycle [2026 United Kingdom local elections - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_Kingdom_local_elections). After the May 2025 county council elections, the Green Party achieved a net gain of 43 seats, bringing their total to 859 councillors across 181 councils [Record high for Green Party after County Council elections](https://greenparty.org.uk/2025/05/03/record-high-for-green-party-after-county-council-elections/). Since then, the party has continued to grow, notably winning the Gorton and Denton parliamentary by-election in February 2026 — its first by-election win [2026 United Kingdom local elections - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_Kingdom_local_elections). April 2026 seat projections from Britain Elects (~1,087 total seats) and More in Common (~1,096 total seats) suggest the Greens could make significant gains [2026 United Kingdom local elections - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_Kingdom_local_elections).

TARGET INFORMATION SET

LATER RESOLUTION PACKET
The resolution criteria require the BBC News “Local Elections 2026” England results page to be used, and require counting the Green Party’s seats won in the 7 May 2026 English local elections, not the party’s overall councillor total after the election. The BBC page was available and complete: it reported that counting was complete after 136 of 136 councils had declared, and its England council results table listed the Green Party with “Councillors Total 587” and “Councillors Change +441” [Local election results 2026 in England - BBC News](https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2026/england/results). Because the question asks for seats won in the election, the relevant BBC figure is the “Councillors Total” for Green, i.e. 587 seats won; the +441 is the change/gain figure, not the number of seats won [Local election results 2026 in England - BBC News](https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2026/england/results).

FORECASTING QUESTION
Will the resolved value be strictly less than 54 percent?

QUANTITY BEING MEASURED
What will the national FAFSA completion rate be for Class of 2026 high school seniors as reported by the NCAN FAFSA Tracker as of its last update on or before June 1, 2026?

RESOLUTION CRITERIA
This question resolves as the national FAFSA completion rate (expressed as a percentage) for the High School Class of 2026, as displayed on the NCAN FAFSA Tracker Tableau dashboard (https://www.ncan.org/Web/Web/FAFSA/FAFSA-Tracker.aspx). The value used will be from the last data update published on or before June 1, 2026. If the tracker is discontinued or unavailable, resolution will be based on the last available snapshot archived or cached before June 1, 2026.

BACKGROUND AVAILABLE AS OF 2026-04-30 12:31:35.141919
The National College Attainment Network (NCAN) publishes a publicly available FAFSA Tracker on Tableau that reports national and state-level FAFSA completion rates for each high school graduating class throughout the filing cycle. As of February 13, 2026, the national FAFSA completion rate for the Class of 2026 stood at 43%. Experts have projected the final rate could reach approximately 56%, which would be an all-time high since NCAN began tracking in 2017. The trajectory depends on late-cycle filing momentum, outreach efforts, and potential policy disruptions at the Department of Education. Historical cycles show completion rates rising significantly between February and June as deadlines approach and school counselors intensify outreach.

TARGET INFORMATION SET
Make a retrospective probability judgment using all information supplied in this prompt, including any LATER RESOLUTION PACKET.

LATER RESOLUTION PACKET
Adjudicated: The criteria binds to the NCAN FAFSA Tracker dashboard value from the last weekly update (Fridays) on or before June 1, 2026 (i.e. May 29). An initial automated figure of 54.7% is provably stale: it is the 'as of May 1' figure repeated across NCAN's May 13 release and downstream coverage, and the rate had already climbed past 55% (over 2.2 million, 'more than 55%') by May 8 and was still rising toward the June 30 benchmark. The 55.4% national rate is the best-attested late-May tracker figure (NAICU Washington Update dated May 22 citing the updated NCAN FAFSA Tracker, plus state outreach posts reproducing 'National: 55.4%'). Confidence is medium because the live Tableau dashboard and Wayback snapshots were not directly readable to confirm the exact May 29 value, but 55.4% is far closer to the binding value than that May 1 number.

TASK
What probability should be assigned to this question resolving YES? Return only one number from 0 to 100.

Therefore, the required month-over-month percent change is 0.5 [[PDF] ADVANCE MONTHLY SALES FOR RETAIL AND FOOD SERVICES ...](https://www.census.gov/retail/marts/www/marts_current.pdf).

The 2026 wildfire season has been extremely active, with 16,746 fires and 1,615,683 acres burned through late April 2026 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_wildfires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_wildfires). Above-normal fire potential is forecast across the Southwest, Great Basin, Northern California, and the Southeast for May–June 2026.

The PL 3 threshold is strategically significant because a new USWFS (United States Wildland Fire Service) policy memo prohibits prescribed fire once a Geographic Area reaches PL 3, making this level a consequential trigger for fire management operations nationwide.

This is a direct statement that the PL never rose above 2 during the entire month of May [[PDF] National Significant Wildland Fire Potential Outlook](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc-files/predictive/outlooks/monthly_seasonal_outlook.pdf).
- The IMSR for the final day of the window, Monday June 1, 2026 (https://www.nifc.gov/nicc-files/sitreprt.pdf), states "National Preparedness Level 2" at the top of the report [[PDF] Incident Management Situation Report Monday June 1, 2026](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc-files/sitreprt.pdf).
- The question description notes the PL started at PL 2 as of April 30, 2026.

Since the PL was 2 at the start of the window, remained at 2 throughout May per the official NIFC monthly outlook, and was still 2 on June 1, 2026, the maximum National Preparedness Level reported in any daily IMSR during the window is 2.

BACKGROUND AVAILABLE AS OF 2026-04-30 12:44:20.404392
ERCOT (Electric Reliability Council of Texas) tracks peak electricity demand across the Texas grid. The current record for May peak demand is 78,399 MW, set on May 23, 2025 [https://www.ercot.com/gridinfo/generation](https://www.ercot.com/gridinfo/generation). According to the ERCOT Monthly Outlook for Resource Adequacy (MORA) for May 2026, the deterministic forecast for peak demand is 65,440 MW at the 50th percentile and 74,557 MW at the 90th percentile (https://www.ercot.com/files/docs/2026/03/06/MORA_May2026.pdf) [https://www.ercot.com/gridinfo/generation](https://www.ercot.com/gridinfo/generation). Actual peak demand depends heavily on weather conditions, particularly early-season heat waves, as well as economic growth and load from new industrial facilities (e.g., data centers) connecting to the grid.

TARGET INFORMATION SET
Make a retrospective probability judgment using all information supplied in this prompt, including any LATER RESOLUTION PACKET.

LATER RESOLUTION PACKET
Adjudicated: ERCOT's peak demand for May 2026 was 77,822 MW, set on May 29, 2026. ERCOT's 2026 peak demand records page carries the May row (77,822 MW, May 29), and the Monthly Operational Overview for May 2026, published June 15, 2026, states that the maximum peak demand for the month was 77,822 MW on 5/29/26, 577 MW below the May 2025 peak of 78,399 MW. ERCOT defines that figure as the maximum net system hourly value from the May 2026 Demand and Energy report, and flags it as preliminary. That report is not the same series as the hourly load archive this question's fallback names, but every ERCOT series available for May 2026 peaks on May 29, and the roughly 29 MW spread between them sits well clear of this question's cutpoint_4 of 77,000. A previous resolution recorded 76,821 MW on the premise that the records page carried no May 2026 entry and that the fallback therefore governed. Monthly entries live on the per-year records page rather than the all-time page, so the entry was present; and the peak fell on May 29, not on the May 31 date that resolution settled for without confirming May 29 or May 30. The correction here is driven by the date, not by the choice of series.

BACKGROUND AVAILABLE AS OF 2026-05-01 17:25:08.324688
The EU AI Act entered into force on August 1, 2024. Under Article 70, member states were required to designate or establish national competent authorities — specifically a market surveillance authority and a notifying authority — by August 2, 2025. As of May 19, 2025, only 3 of 27 EU member states had clearly designated both authorities, while 10 had partial clarity (e.g., pending legislative proposals or one authority appointed) and 14 remained unclear [https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/national-implementation-plans/](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/national-implementation-plans/). Member states have historically been slow to meet EU implementation deadlines, as seen with GDPR. The question tracks how many will have completed formal designation by June 1, 2026 — approximately 10 months past the original deadline.

Make a retrospective probability judgment using all information supplied in this prompt, including any LATER RESOLUTION PACKET.

LATER RESOLUTION PACKET

The EC 'Market Surveillance Authorities under the AI Act' list (the portal's operative published designation list) shows 8 member states notified: Cyprus, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Slovenia, and Spain. The official EPRS 'Enforcement of the AI Act' briefing (18 March 2026) independently confirms 'eight single contact points, out of 27,' a figure corroborated by secondary trackers through May 2026, with no source indicating any increase before 1 June 2026. An initial automated answer of '0' wrongly required a separately published notifying-authority list that the portal does not maintain; the portal's published SPOC/market-surveillance list of 8 is the operative fallback count.

The Roraima supplementary governor election was held on June 21, 2026. The candidate with the highest vote total in the first round was Arthur Henrique (PL), with 160,004 votes, which corresponds to 60.87% of valid votes (votos válidos).

Evidence:
- The official Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) notice, "Arthur Henrique é o mais votado para o cargo de governador na eleição suplementar de Roraima" (https://www.tse.jus.br/comunicacao/noticias/2026/Junho/arthur-henrique-e-o-mais-votado-para-o-cargo-de-governador-na-eleicao-suplementar-de-roraima), reports Arthur Henrique as the most voted candidate with 160,004 votes = 60.87% of valid votes; Soldado Sampaio (Republicanos) second with 93,897 votes = 35.72%; Nelita Frank (PT) with 8,948 votes = 3.40% [Arthur Henrique é o mais votado para o cargo de governador na ...](https://www.tse.jus.br/comunicacao/noticias/2026/Junho/arthur-henrique-e-o-mais-votado-para-o-cargo-de-governador-na-eleicao-suplementar-de-roraima).
- G1, reporting TRE-RR data with 100% of ballots counted, gives the identical figures: Arthur Henrique 160,004 (60.87%), Soldado Sampaio 93,897 (35.72%), Nelita Frank 8,948 (3.40%) (https://g1.globo.com/rr/roraima/noticia/2026/06/21/arthur-henrique-e-o-mais-votado-para-governador-em-eleicao-suplementar-de-roraima.ghtml) [Arthur Henrique é mais votado para governador em eleição sub ...](https://g1.globo.com/rr/roraima/noticia/2026/06/21/arthur-henrique-e-o-mais-votado-para-governador-em-eleicao-suplementar-de-roraima.ghtml).
- The Portuguese Wikipedia results table confirms the same totals and percentages, citing the official TSE results portal (resultados.tse.jus.br) [Eleição suplementar para governador de Roraima em 2026](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elei%C3%A7%C3%A3o_suplementar_para_governador_de_Roraima_em_2026).

Arithmetic check: 160,004 + 93,897 + 8,948 = 262,849 total valid votes; 160,004 / 262,849 = 60.87%, consistent with the reported figure.

Note on the sub judice status: Arthur Henrique's candidacy registration was rejected by the TRE-RR and remained under appeal (sub judice) at the time of the count, so he was not proclaimed elected [Arthur Henrique é o mais votado para o cargo de governador na ...](https://www.tse.jus.br/comunicacao/noticias/2026/Junho/arthur-henrique-e-o-mais-votado-para-o-cargo-de-governador-na-eleicao-suplementar-de-roraima)[Arthur Henrique é mais votado para governador em eleição sub ...](https://g1.globo.com/rr/roraima/noticia/2026/06/21/arthur-henrique-e-o-mais-votado-para-governador-em-eleicao-suplementar-de-roraima.ghtml). However, the resolution criteria asks specifically for "the percentage of valid votes received by the candidate with the highest vote total in the first round." Under Brazilian electoral law (Art. 16-A of Law 9.504/1997), a sub judice candidate's votes are counted normally in the official totalization, and the official TSE/TRE-RR totalization reported Arthur Henrique with 60.87% of valid votes. His votes were therefore treated as valid in the official count. The "39.13%" figure appearing in one source is merely the combined share of the other two candidates (93,897 + 8,948 = 102,845; 102,845/262,849 = 39.13%), a hypothetical used to describe what would remain if his votes were later annulled — it is not Arthur Henrique's share [Eleição suplementar para governador de Roraima em 2026](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elei%C3%A7%C3%A3o_suplementar_para_governador_de_Roraima_em_2026).

Therefore, the top candidate received 60.87% of valid votes. Units are "percent," so the value is reported as 60.87.

admissible_variant.with_information_prompt:
FORECASTING QUESTION
Will the resolved value be strictly less than 70000 acres?

QUANTITY BEING MEASURED
How many acres will the largest single wildfire in the United States burn between May 1 and June 1, 2026?

RESOLUTION CRITERIA
This question resolves as the number of acres burned by the largest single wildfire incident in the United States that was active at any point between May 1, 2026, and June 1, 2026 (inclusive of both dates).

Key definitions and rules:

1. **Single wildfire:** A wildfire tracked as a single incident in the NIFC IRWIN (Integrated Reporting of Wildland Fire Information) system. Fire complexes — multiple fires managed under a single incident command — count as a single incident only if they are assigned a single IRWIN identifier. If individual fires within a complex retain separate IRWIN identifiers, each is counted separately.

2. **Acreage measured:** The total reported acreage of the fire as of the NIFC Incident Management Situation Report (IMSR) published closest to but not after June 1, 2026. This includes all acres the fire has burned over its entire lifetime up to that report date, not just acres burned during the May 1–June 1 window.

3. **Eligibility:** Any wildfire that was reported as active in any IMSR published between May 1, 2026, and June 1, 2026, qualifies — regardless of when the fire originally started. This includes fires that started before May 1 but remained active during the window.

4. **Fires active past June 1:** If a fire remains active beyond June 1, 2026, the acreage figure used is the one reported in the last IMSR published on or before June 1, 2026.

5. **Resolution source:** The NIFC Incident Management Situation Report (IMSR), available at https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/incident-information/imsr. InciWeb (https://inciweb.wildfire.gov) and the NIFC WFIGS perimeter data (https://data-nifc.opendata.arcgis.com) may be used as supplementary sources if the IMSR does not provide sufficient detail.

6. **If no wildfire exceeding 100 acres is active during the window**, the question resolves as 0.

"Participants" refers to all FOMC meeting attendees (up to 19 Federal Reserve officials: 7 Board of Governors members and 12 Reserve Bank presidents), not just the 12 voting members.

The count will be determined by the qualitative language used in the minutes as follows:
- "A couple" = 2
- "A few" = 3
- "Several" = 4-5 (resolve as 4 unless additional context clarifies)
- "Some" = 3-5 (resolve as 4 unless additional context clarifies)
- "Many" = 6-8 (resolve as 7 unless additional context clarifies)
- "Most" = more than half (resolve as 12 unless additional context clarifies)

What will the INPE DETER deforestation alert area for the Brazilian Amazon be in April 2026?

RESOLUTION CRITERIA
This question resolves as the total deforestation alert area (in square kilometers) for the Legal Amazon (Amazônia Legal) for the month of April 2026, as reported by the INPE (National Institute for Space Research) DETER system. The official value will be obtained from the TerraBrasilis platform (https://terrabrasilis.dpi.inpe.br/app/dashboard/alerts/legal/amazon/monthly/). INPE typically publishes monthly DETER data within the first two weeks of the following month. If the data is subsequently revised, the first officially published monthly figure will be used for resolution.

BACKGROUND AVAILABLE AS OF 2026-04-30 17:50:51.095305
The Brazilian National Institute for Space Research (INPE) operates the DETER (Real-Time Deforestation Detection) system, which uses satellite imagery to issue near-real-time alerts for deforestation and forest degradation in the Legal Amazon (Amazônia Legal). Monthly alert data is published on the TerraBrasilis platform.

In April 2025, the DETER system recorded approximately 270 square kilometers of deforestation alerts in the Amazon, a 55% increase compared to April 2024 [Desmatamento cresce 55% na Amazônia em abril, diz instituto](https://www.poder360.com.br/poder-sustentavel/desmatamento-cresce-55-na-amazonia-em-abril-diz-instituto/). However, the broader trend has been strongly downward: between August 2025 and January 2026, cumulative deforestation alerts fell 35% year-over-year, reaching the lowest levels since 2014 [Deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon increases by 7.3% in ...](https://noticiasambientales.com/environment-en/deforestation-in-the-brazilian-amazon-increases-by-7-3-in-february-impacting-the-forest-mass/). In February 2026, DETER registered 95.4 square kilometers of deforestation alerts, a 7.3% year-over-year increase — the first such reversal in months, breaking the pattern of consistent declines [Deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon increases by 7.3% in ...](https://noticiasambientales.com/environment-en/deforestation-in-the-brazilian-amazon-increases-by-7-3-in-february-impacting-the-forest-mass/).

April falls near the transition between the wet and dry seasons in the Amazon. Cloud cover variability during this period can significantly affect satellite detection capability, introducing noise into monthly figures regardless of actual deforestation activity. The interplay between ongoing enforcement efforts under Brazil's current deforestation policies and seasonal weather patterns will be key factors influencing the April 2026 figure.

TARGET INFORMATION SET
Make a retrospective probability judgment using all information supplied in this prompt, including any LATER RESOLUTION PACKET.

LATER RESOLUTION PACKET
Adjudicated: INPE DETER recorded 228 km2 of deforestation alerts in the Legal Amazon for April 2026, a 15% year-over-year decrease from the 270 km2 of April 2025. This figure is reported consistently and independently by ClimaInfo (May 10, 2026) and Folha de S.Paulo / acessa.com (May 8, 2026), both explicitly attributing it to the INPE DETER system that the resolution criteria designate (TerraBrasilis). The companion Cerrado figures (691->418 km2, -40%) match across the same sources, and 270 x 0.85 ~= 228 confirms internal consistency. An initial automated figure of 175 km2 came only from unverifiable social-media posts and is contradicted by all credible news reporting.

What will the first-preference vote percentage be for the winner of the 2026 Washington, D.C. Democratic mayoral primary?

RESOLUTION CRITERIA
This question resolves as the percentage of first-preference votes received by the winning candidate in the 2026 Washington, D.C. Democratic mayoral primary, as reported by the District of Columbia Board of Elections (DCBOE) in their official certified results for the June 16, 2026 primary election (available at https://electionresults.dcboe.org/). "First-preference votes" are defined as the votes cast for a candidate as the voter's top choice (i.e., their first-ranked selection) before any RCV reallocation rounds occur. The resolution value is calculated as: (first-preference votes for the winning candidate) ÷ (total first-preference votes cast for all candidates in the Democratic mayoral primary) × 100, expressed as a percentage. The "winner" is the candidate ultimately certified as the Democratic nominee by DCBOE, regardless of whether they won on the first round or after RCV reallocation.

BACKGROUND AVAILABLE AS OF 2026-05-29 03:08:43.653470
The 2026 Washington, D.C. Democratic mayoral primary is scheduled for June 16, 2026, and will be the first election in D.C. to use ranked-choice voting (RCV). The race features two leading candidates—Janeese Lewis George (progressive/labor) and Kenyan McDuffie (establishment/business)—along with several minor candidates. In the most recent 2022 Democratic mayoral primary, incumbent Muriel Bowser won with 49.01% of the vote [2022 Washington, D.C., mayoral election - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Washington,_D.C.,_mayoral_election). The introduction of RCV means that if no candidate exceeds 50% of first-preference votes, lower-ranked candidates are eliminated and their votes reallocated until a winner emerges. The presence of multiple candidates in 2026 could fragment first-preference votes, making it uncertain whether the eventual winner will secure a majority on the first count. An RFK Stadium ballot initiative on the same June 16 ballot could also affect turnout dynamics.

TARGET INFORMATION SET
Make a retrospective probability judgment using all information supplied in this prompt, including any LATER RESOLUTION PACKET.

LATER RESOLUTION PACKET
WINNER: Janeese Lewis George won the 2026 Washington, D.C. Democratic mayoral primary (held June 16, 2026); Kenyan McDuffie conceded and she was named the Democratic nominee (multiple outlets, and she led on first-preference votes so no RCV reallocation was needed — she cleared a majority in Round 1).

SOURCE (as specified): The District of Columbia Board of Elections (DCBOE) results at https://electionresults.dcboe.org/election_results/2026-Primary-Election. For the "DEM MAYOR OF THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA" contest, the first-rank (first-preference) vote counts are [DCBOE Primary and Special Election 2026 Election Results](https://electionresults.dcboe.org/election_results/2026-Primary-Election) [DCBOE Primary and Special Election 2026 Election Results](https://electionresults.dcboe.org/election_results/2026-Primary-Election):
- Janeese Lewis George: 75,591 (DCBOE-reported 54.06%)
- Kenyan R. McDuffie: 49,139 (35.15%)
- Rini Sampath: 4,483 (3.21%)
- Gary Goodweather: 4,383 (3.13%)
- Vincent Orange ("VO"): 3,563 (2.55%)
- Hope Solomon: 1,487 (1.06%)
- Ernest E. Johnson: 711 (0.51%)
- Write-in: 460 (0.33%)

CALCULATION per the resolution criteria: numerator = winner's first-preference votes (75,591); denominator = total first-preference votes for all candidates. Summing the eight lines above = 139,817 (DCBOE's page states 139,818, a 1-vote rounding/typo). 75,591 ÷ 139,817 × 100 = 54.06%. This exactly matches the 54.06% DCBOE itself reports for George, and the listed candidate percentages sum to 100.00%, confirming the denominator includes all candidates plus write-ins.

CAVEAT ON "CERTIFIED": The DCBOE page currently labels these figures "Election Night Unofficial Results," last updated June 25, 2026 [DCBOE Primary and Special Election 2026 Election Results](https://electionresults.dcboe.org/election_results/2026-Primary-Election). Per the DCBOE 2026 Primary Election Calendar, certification is tentatively scheduled for July 17, 2026 [[PDF] June 16, 2026 Primary Election Calendar of Important Dates and ...](https://dcboe.org/getmedia/3a7e75bc-4a1b-4aa6-9fc3-f30163beb2b5/2026-Primary-Election-Calendar-Version-08072025.pdf), which is after the latest data I could access (my web access reflects ~late June/early July 2026). Certified totals may add a handful of late-counted provisional/mail ballots, but this June 25 count is essentially final (9 days post-election, McDuffie already conceded) and any change to the winner's percentage would be trivial. I therefore report 54.06.

NOTE ON ALTERNATIVE FIGURES: Wikipedia's article table showed slightly lower/earlier numbers (George 74,878 of 138,616 = 54.02%) [2026 Washington, D.C., mayoral election - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Washington,_D.C.,_mayoral_election), and FairVote rounded to "54%" [Preliminary results from the first ranked choice voting election in ...](https://fairvote.org/preliminary-results-from-the-first-ranked-choice-voting-election-in-washington-dc/). I prefer the direct DCBOE figures (the criteria's named source), which are the most complete count; the small difference reflects Wikipedia using an earlier snapshot.

Platner has consistently led in polling throughout the race, though he has faced some controversies regarding past social media posts and a tattoo [2026 United States Senate election in Maine - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_election_in_Maine). RESULT: Graham Platner received ~72.2% of the vote among named ballot candidates in the June 9, 2026 Maine Democratic U.S. Senate primary.

CERTIFIED VOTE TOTALS (official results published by Maine Secretary of State; mirrored by AP and reported in the Wikipedia results table [2026 United States Senate election in Maine - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_election_in_Maine) [2026 United States Senate election in Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_election_in_Maine)):
- Graham Platner: 154,058
- Janet Mills: 41,301
- David Costello: 17,871
- Andrea LaFlamme (write-in): 1,052
- Total shown: 214,282

The official Maine Secretary of State certification file is "US Senate DEM - FINAL.xlsx" hosted at https://www.maine.gov/sos/sites/maine.gov.sos/files/inline-files/US%20Senate%20DEM%20-%20FINAL.xlsx (linked from the SoS results index https://www.maine.gov/sos/cec/elec/results/index.html) [https://www.maine.gov/sos/cec/elec/results/index.html](https://www.maine.gov/sos/cec/elec/results/index.html). (Automated parsing of that .xlsx returned inconsistent/erroneous figures — e.g., 48,214 for Platner and 'Mills=0/not on ballot' [https://www.maine.gov/sos/sites/maine.gov.sos/files/inline-files/US%20Senate%20DEM%20-%20FINAL.xlsx](https://www.maine.gov/sos/sites/maine.gov.sos/files/inline-files/US%20Senate%20DEM%20-%20FINAL.xlsx) [https://www.maine.gov/sos/sites/maine.gov.sos/files/inline-files/US%20Senate%20DEM%20-%20FINAL.xlsx](https://www.maine.gov/sos/sites/maine.gov.sos/files/inline-files/US%20Senate%20DEM%20-%20FINAL.xlsx) — which directly contradict every reliable narrative source and the internally-consistent AP/Wikipedia table, so those spreadsheet-parse numbers were rejected as parsing failures. The Senate race did NOT appear among the five June 9 races that required a ranked-choice tabulation [Maine Secretary of State's Office announces ranked choice ...](https://www.maine.gov/sos/news/maine-secretary-states-office-announces-ranked-choice-tabulations), confirming Platner won an outright first-round majority.)

CRITICAL POINT — JANET MILLS WAS ON THE BALLOT: Although Gov. Janet Mills suspended her campaign on April 30, 2026, her name REMAINED PRINTED on the primary ballot. Maine law requires a withdrawal notice 70 days before a primary to remove a name, and Mills suspended only ~40 days out, so she stayed on the ballot and her votes counted. This is confirmed by Politico ("she remained on the ballot") [Graham Platner wins Maine Democratic Senate primary to ... - Politico](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/09/graham-platner-wins-maine-senate-primary-00955484), 270towin (notes Mills remained on the ballot despite suspending) [2026 Maine Primary Live Results - 270toWin.com](https://www.270towin.com/2026-election-results-live/state/maine/primary), and corroborated by WGME, the Press Herald ("I am still on the ballot"), and the Maine Monitor (explaining the 70-day rule).

APPLYING THE RESOLUTION CRITERIA: The criteria define the value as (votes for Platner) ÷ (total votes cast for all NAMED candidates on the ballot), excluding ONLY write-in votes and blank/spoiled ballots. Mills was a named candidate on the ballot, so her votes are neither write-ins nor blank/spoiled and MUST be included in the denominator. Write-in LaFlamme (1,052) is excluded.
- Denominator = 154,058 + 41,301 + 17,871 = 213,230
- Platner % = 154,058 ÷ 213,230 = 0.72250 = 72.25%, which rounds to 72.2%.

NOTE ON THE QUESTION DESCRIPTION: The description (written May 13, 2026) mistakenly listed only David Costello (plus write-in LaFlamme) as remaining ballot candidates, implicitly assuming Mills had left the ballot. That assumption was factually wrong — Mills stayed on the ballot. The literal resolution criteria (which supersede the description) count all named ballot candidates, so Mills is included. Had Mills instead been (incorrectly) excluded, the figure would be 154,058 ÷ (154,058+17,871) = 89.6%; this alternative is rejected because it violates the literal criteria.

This question resolves as the largest single-day intraday range (daily high minus daily low) observed on the ICE Brent Crude front-month futures contract (ticker "B" on ICE Futures Europe) across all trading days in May 2026 (May 1 through May 31, inclusive of any days on which trading occurs).

**Front-month contract definition:** The front-month contract is the nearest-expiry contract with open interest that has not yet expired. If a contract rollover occurs during May 2026 (i.e., the nearest contract expires and the next contract becomes the front-month), each trading day's range is measured on whichever contract is the front-month on that day. The July 2026 (BRN26) contract is expected to be the front-month for most or all of May 2026, as the June 2026 contract expires in late April.

**Source:** Daily high and daily low prices as reported by the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) for the Brent Crude Futures contract (https://www.ice.com/products/219/Brent-Crude-Futures). If ICE data is unavailable or not publicly accessible, Investing.com Brent Oil Futures historical data (https://www.investing.com/commodities/brent-oil-historical-data) may be used as a secondary source.

**Price fields:** The daily high and daily low prices for the front-month contract as recorded during the full ICE trading session (01:00–23:00 GMT, or 20:00–18:00 ET the following day).

**Calculation:** For each trading day in May 2026, compute (daily high − daily low). The question resolves as the maximum of these values across all May 2026 trading days, in USD per barrel.

If IMF PortWatch data is unavailable or discontinued, the question resolves ambiguously.

What will the Magyar Nemzeti Bank's (MNB) June 2026 Inflation Report forecast for 2026 annual average inflation be?

RESOLUTION CRITERIA
This question resolves to the annual average consumer price index (CPI) inflation forecast for 2026, as published in the Magyar Nemzeti Bank's June 2026 Inflation Report. The specific figure is the baseline projection point estimate for 2026 average annual inflation, as shown in the report's summary table of macroeconomic forecasts. The report is expected to be published on or around June 23–26, 2026 on the MNB's official website (https://www.mnb.hu). If the report provides a range rather than a single point estimate, the midpoint of that range will be used. If the June 2026 Inflation Report is not published by July 1, 2026, the question resolves ambiguously.

BACKGROUND AVAILABLE AS OF 2026-05-14 03:48:01.242249
The Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) publishes quarterly Inflation Reports containing macroeconomic forecasts. The MNB's inflation target is 3%, with a tolerance band of 2–4%. In the March 2026 Inflation Report, the MNB revised its 2026 annual average inflation forecast upward to 3.8% from the previous 3.2%, primarily due to energy price increases driven by the Iran conflict [https://www.mnb.hu/en/monetary-policy/the-monetary-council/press-releases/2026/press-release-on-the-monetary-council-meeting-of-28-april-2026](https://www.mnb.hu/en/monetary-policy/the-monetary-council/press-releases/2026/press-release-on-the-monetary-council-meeting-of-28-april-2026). The 2027 forecast was also raised to 3.7% from 3.3%. As of March 2026, actual year-over-year inflation stood at 1.8%, with core inflation at 1.9% [https://www.mnb.hu/en/monetary-policy/the-monetary-council/press-releases/2026/press-release-on-the-monetary-council-meeting-of-28-april-2026](https://www.mnb.hu/en/monetary-policy/the-monetary-council/press-releases/2026/press-release-on-the-monetary-council-meeting-of-28-april-2026). The MNB has held its base rate at 6.5% since September 2024. The June 2026 Inflation Report will incorporate several additional months of data on energy prices, forint exchange rate movements, and domestic price pressures, and will be finalized around the June 23, 2026 Monetary Council meeting [https://www.mnb.hu/en/monetary-policy/the-monetary-council/press-releases/2026/press-release-on-the-monetary-council-meeting-of-28-april-2026](https://www.mnb.hu/en/monetary-policy/the-monetary-council/press-releases/2026/press-release-on-the-monetary-council-meeting-of-28-april-2026).

Make a retrospective probability judgment using all information supplied in this prompt, including any LATER RESOLUTION PACKET.

LATER RESOLUTION PACKET
The MNB's June 2026 Inflation Report baseline projection for 2026 annual average CPI inflation is 1.8 percent.

Evidence:
- The MNB's own "Baseline inflation and GDP projection of the June 2026 Inflation Report" fan-chart summary document (https://www.mnb.hu/letoltes/honlapra-fanchart-en-34.pdf) lists the baseline point estimates for annual average inflation as 2026: 1.8%, 2027: 2.3%, 2028: 3.0%. The projections are based on information available through 18 June 2026 [Baseline inflation and GDP projection of the June 2026 ...](https://www.mnb.hu/letoltes/honlapra-fanchart-en-34.pdf).
- The MNB press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 23 June 2026 (https://www.mnb.hu/en/monetary-policy/the-monetary-council/press-releases/2026/press-release-on-the-monetary-council-meeting-of-23-june-2026) states explicitly: "On annual average, inflation will be 1.8 percent this year, 2.3 percent in 2027, and 3.0 percent in 2028." This confirms the 2026 figure of 1.8% and dates the report/finalization to 23 June 2026 [https://www.mnb.hu/en/monetary-policy/the-monetary-council/press-releases/2026/press-release-on-the-monetary-council-meeting-of-23-june-2026](https://www.mnb.hu/en/monetary-policy/the-monetary-council/press-releases/2026/press-release-on-the-monetary-council-meeting-of-23-june-2026).

Both sources agree; the report was published on 23 June 2026, before the July 1, 2026 cutoff, so the question resolves numerically (not ambiguously). The value is a single point estimate (not a range), so no midpointing is required. Third-party corroboration (OTP Bank commentary, June 2026) also cites the MNB baseline of 1.8% for 2026 and 2.3% for 2027.

Note: This 1.8% is a sharp downward revision from the 3.8% forecast in the March 2026 Inflation Report referenced in the question description.

The settled count is 6, made up of two distinct parliamentary votes:

BATCH 1 — May 8, 2025 (5 ministers): The National Assembly adopted mise en accusation resolutions (115+ of 126 deputies in favor for each) referring five Macky Sall-era ministers: Moustapha Diop (Industrial Development), Amadou Mansour Faye (Community Development), Aïssatou Sophie Gladima (Mines and Geology), Ismaïla Madior Fall (Justice), and Salimata Diop / Ndèye Saly Diop (Women/Family). Confirmed by Anadolu Agency [Sénégal : Cinq anciens ministres de Macky Sall envoyés devant la ...](https://www.aa.com.tr/fr/afrique/s%C3%A9n%C3%A9gal-cinq-anciens-ministres-de-macky-sall-envoy%C3%A9s-devant-la-haute-cour-de-justice/3562321) and RFI's May 8, 2025 report [Sénégal: cinq ministres de l'ex-président Macky Sall renvoyés ... - RFI](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20250508-s%C3%A9n%C3%A9gal-cinq-ministres-de-l-ex-pr%C3%A9sident-macky-sall-renvoy%C3%A9s-devant-la-haute-cour-de-justice). This is corroborated by Le Monde, France24, Jeune Afrique and magazineregards, which all report "cinq ministres renvoyés devant la Haute Cour de justice."

BATCH 2 — Feb 27, 2026 (1 minister): The National Assembly plenary voted (104 votes in favor, per Dakaractu) the mise en accusation of Moussa Bocar Thiam (Communications and Digital Affairs). RFI's Feb 28, 2026 article explicitly describes him as the SIXTH former Macky Sall minister referred to the High Court of Justice since 2025 [Sénégal: un ex-ministre de Macky Sall renvoyé devant la Haute ...](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20260228-s%C3%A9n%C3%A9gal-un-ex-ministre-de-macky-sall-renvoy%C3%A9-devant-la-haute-cour-de-justice), and the RFI/Yahoo wire version repeats "le sixième ministre ... à être traduit devant la Haute Cour de Justice sénégalaise, depuis 2025" [un ex-ministre de Macky Sall renvoyé devant la Haute Cour de Justice](https://fr.news.yahoo.com/s%C3%A9n%C3%A9gal-ex-ministre-macky-sall-113519182.html). The APS and Africanews reports confirm the formal parliamentary vote occurred Feb 27, 2026.

EXCLUSIONS: A seventh potential case — Abdoulaye Diouf Sarr (former Health Minister) — was examined by the Law Commission on Feb 23, 2026 alongside Thiam, but his file was blocked/returned for complément d'information because the documents were incomplete; it never reached a full National Assembly referral vote [Assemblée nationale : La commission des lois vote la mise en ...](https://www.dakaractu.com/Assemblee-nationale-La-commission-des-lois-vote-la-mise-en-accusation-de-Moussa-Bocar-Thiam-le-dossier-Diouf-Sarr_a269398.html). Under the resolution criteria (committee-stage cases do not count), Diouf Sarr is excluded. No additional (7th) referral by formal National Assembly vote was found between March 1 and July 1, 2026; that period was dominated by other events (Sonko dismissed as PM May 22, elected NA president May 26, new government June 1, constitutional revision June 29). June 2026 news about Mansour Faye concerned the commission d'instruction (investigation) stage of a minister already referred in May 2025, not a new referral.

RECONCILING THE DISCREPANCY: The question description states "at least 5" as of Feb 2026 (citing Africanews, which says "at least five"), and one Voxafrica Facebook post called Thiam the "cinquième." These are undercounts/loose reporting. The higher-quality RFI reporting explicitly and repeatedly states Thiam is the SIXTH [Sénégal: un ex-ministre de Macky Sall renvoyé devant la Haute ...](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20260228-s%C3%A9n%C3%A9gal-un-ex-ministre-de-macky-sall-renvoy%C3%A9-devant-la-haute-cour-de-justice) [un ex-ministre de Macky Sall renvoyé devant la Haute Cour de Justice](https://fr.news.yahoo.com/s%C3%A9n%C3%A9gal-ex-ministre-macky-sall-113519182.html), consistent with the arithmetic 5 (May 2025) + 1 (Feb 2026) = 6, all six being distinct, named Macky Sall-era ministers.

Units are "ministers"; the answer on that scale is 6.
